name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS. Notification exposes a full diagnosis on Lock Screen, repeats every minute after dismissal and opens the generic home screen. Acknowledging a reminder incorrectly cancels the appointment. Permission may be denied.

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and

name: apple-hig-notifications
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting notification content, previews, actions, badges, foreground treatment, and watch looks.

# Make the notification useful before opening the app

Read [the notification guide](../../references/notifications.md). This workflow is application advice; delivery remains subject to consent and system/user settings.

Inspect event value/timeliness, consent/category, sensitive content, foreground context, actions, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Distinguish communication from generic updates and one event from duplicate reminders. Record real badge/account/action state; do not assume delivery or permission from mock notification text.

Write concise contextual titles/bodies with a generic private-preview description. Avoid repeating app identity or exposing confidential details. Provide useful simple actions with outcome labels and no redundant Open App; mark consequential destruction. Keep essential meaning independent of sound. In foreground integrate updates into the current UI instead of duplicating interruption. Badge unread notifications only, update/clear addressed counts promptly, and preserve an in-app route when badges are disabled.

Implement content/category/action/badge handling or supply an event-to-presentation contract; reviews identify exact disclosure, duplication, or action defects. On watch short looks must be discreet, long looks preserve system structure and static fallback, and the likely nondestructive first action should fit supported double tap. Do not promise custom vibration through this guidance.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a banking notification exposes an account balance on Lock Screen, badges show the balance, and `Open App` repeats ordinary activation. Decision: private data and badge semantics are misused. After: provide a generic transaction category when previews hide, use unread count only, and offer a truly useful safe action or rely on precise ordinary activation.

Deliver the artifact, preview-hidden text, actions/deep links, foreground behavior, and badge lifecycle. Verify locked previews, duplicate events, action resolution, addressed counts, and watch fallback where relevant. Fail for confidential exposure, unrelated badge values, duplicate interruption, or wrong-object action. Separate native delivery/permission/sound checks from inspected logic.

Load [managing-notifications](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-managing-notifications/SKILL.md) for permission/urgency strategy or [alerts](../../../apple-hig-presentation/.topics/apple-hig-alerts/SKILL.md) for immediate error resolution.

name: apple-hig-managing-notifications
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting notification permission, urgency, Focus behavior, and informational or marketing preferences.
---

# Preserve the person's control over interruption

Read [the notification-management guide](../../references/managing-notifications.md). The workflow is application advice; delivery levels and entitlements are source constraints, not guaranteed delivery.

Inspect event categories, personal impact/timing, consent history, preference UI, platform, and create/review/adapt mode. Distinguish communication from noncommunication and marketing from requested information. Record permission/entitlement evidence; do not infer it from an urgent-looking mockup.

Request consent and respect later silencing/Focus/summary choices. Assign Passive/Active/Time Sensitive/Critical from real urgency rather than business attention goals. Time Sensitive concerns immediate personal impact now/within an hour and remains user-controllable; Critical needs the entitlement and an actual urgent health/safety case. Marketing requires separate explicit content-specific opt-in with accept/decline and must never be Time Sensitive. Provide in-app settings for informational/marketing preferences without pretending they override system settings. Use sender-based supported communication integration when relevant. Watch generally follows companion settings with its documented controls.

Implement authorized category/permission/settings behavior, specify an event/urgency/consent matrix, or review exact overclassification and consent defects. Do not send actual notifications merely to demonstrate a proposed policy without authorization.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a shopping app labels every discount Time Sensitive after a generic permission prompt and offers no marketing opt-out. Decision: sales urgency is not immediate personal impact and permission is not specific marketing consent. After: use appropriate ordinary delivery only after explicit promotional opt-in, with independent preference changes and respect for Focus.

Deliver the artifact, event rationale, interruption level, consent source, and preference routes. Verify denied/revoked permission, Focus, opt-out, nonresponding recipients, and entitlement absence. Fail for marketing breakthrough, implied guaranteed delivery, or inaccessible preference withdrawal. Native Focus/delivery/entitlement execution requires separate evidence.

Load [notifications](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-notifications/SKILL.md) for content/actions or [privacy](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for consent and exposure.

name: apple-hig-privacy
description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.
---

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

For health-related work, finish the domain decisions as well as the permission
sequence. Read [CareKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-carekit/SKILL.md)
for care plans, scheduled treatment tasks, or symptom/event recording;
[HealthKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-healthkit/SKILL.md)
for health-data access and sharing; and
[ResearchKit](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-researchkit/SKILL.md)
for study participation and research consent. These experience procedures help
choose task, data, and consent behavior in the existing stack; consulting a
framework-named topic does not require adopting that SDK. General privacy,
language, and accessibility guidance alone does not resolve those domain choices.

name: apple-hig-writing
description: Use when drafting or reviewing interface labels, instructions, empty states, errors, settings, or other product language for Apple-platform tasks.
---

# Write the action and the remedy people need

Read [Writing](../../references/writing.md). Inspect the actual flow, terminology, audience, component, device/input, and requested design/review/adaptation scope. Preserve product meaning and existing voice while changing copy. If a screenshot omits the triggering behavior, qualify the interpretation rather than inventing an error cause.

Identify the person's current question: what happened, what can I do, or what should I enter? Put that information first. Use clear action verbs and link destinations; keep terminology/capitalization consistent across entry, continuation, and completion. Adjust seriousness to context without changing the product's identity. Name the correct input action for the target device rather than telling a TV viewer to tap.

Choose the surface along with the words. An ordinary correction belongs near its field; urgent required attention may justify an alert. Label every field and provide usable formats/examples. If an error repeats, inspect whether the interaction can prevent it before polishing the message. Empty states should offer a useful next action, but essential permanent instructions should not exist only before content arrives. Settings should describe their enabled behavior and link directly where possible.

Remove needless words, ambiguous responsibility, perspective shifts, and culture-bound cleverness. Read revised copy aloud and check it in the actual component; concise wording that conceals consequences is not an improvement. Consider screen-reader access and shared/distant displays.

**Before → decision → after:** A booking form says “Oops! Invalid” after rejecting a time, with “Click here” below. Decision: the person needs the permitted time and an action. After, a nearby message reads “Choose a time between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM,” and the control says “Choose another time.” The same term “appointment” persists through confirmation.

Deliver replacement strings in context or the updated artifact, explaining meaningful behavioral assumptions. Fail if a label hides its outcome, correction still gives no remedy, or translation/large text removes essential meaning. Source review establishes wording, not actual localized pronunciation or screen-reader behavior unless tested.

Use [Inclusion](../apple-hig-inclusion/SKILL.md) for assumptions and representation, [Privacy](../apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for purpose strings, or [Accessibility](../apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for semantic access.

# Notifications Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/notifications) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Notifications deliver timely high-value information after consent. People control styles, urgency, delivery, previews, sound, and badges through system settings. ## Anatomy Notifications can appear as banners, Lock/Home/desktop views, badges, and Notification Center entries. Direct communications can emphasize a sender or group image/name instead of the ordinary app-icon treatment. ## Best practices Keep updates concise and useful; do not repeat the same event because the person has not responded. Avoid instructions that require remembering a later app task; offer an immediate action when useful. Use alerts for error situations. In the foreground, integrate incoming information subtly into the current UI instead of duplicating it with an interruption. Do not expose confidential, personal, or sensitive details to nearby observers. ## Content Use a brief title only when it adds context; direct communications use the sender's name, and generic noncommunication titles can defer to the app name. Titles use title case without punctuation. Bodies use short complete sentences with sentence case/punctuation; leave truncation to the system. Provide a generic preview-hidden description that conveys category without private details. Do not repeat app name or icon because the system supplies them, including a small app badge on communication avatars. Sound can reinforce identity but cannot be the sole essential signal. Custom sounds should be brief, distinctive, and well produced; custom vibration alongside them is not programmatically available through this guidance. ## Notification actions Offer up to four simple useful actions that save opening the app. Use short title-case outcome labels and recognizable glyphs, without app branding or filler. Do not add an Open App button when ordinary notification activation already opens its related content. Prefer nondestructive actions; mark and adequately contextualize any destructive one. ## Badging Use badge numbers for unread notifications, never unrelated temperatures, dates, prices, or scores. Clear/update them promptly when notifications are addressed; a count of zero removes related entries from Notification Center. Keep important information discoverable in the app because badges can be disabled. Do not imitate badges with a custom component to bypass that preference. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Watch delivery uses short and long looks and Notification Center. A companion iPhone app can supply default watch interfaces; custom relevant assets/actions improve the result. #### Short looks Raised-wrist short looks disappear when the wrist lowers. Keep them discreet and basic, especially the title, and deliver critical information elsewhere too because this presentation is brief. #### Long looks Long looks offer more detail and scroll with touch or crown, dismissing on tap or lowered wrist. Static views include a message plus prepared text/images; dynamic views access full notification content. Keep the system sash and bottom Dismiss structure. Always package a static fallback for offline/unreachable-companion cases and prefer a dynamic view too. Rich custom content and interruptible animation can avoid opening the app. Tint or blur the sash; blur suits a top photo. Content defaults transparent; white at 18% opacity matches system notification backgrounds, or use a suitable custom color. Up to four custom buttons appear above the fixed Dismiss action; companion notification categories can configure them. #### Double tap Supported watches invoke the first nondestructive action for double tap. Place the most likely response first, such as the commonly chosen time extension. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Managing notifications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications) [Alerts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts) #### Developer documentation — User Notifications #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: October 24, 2023.

# Managing notifications Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Request permission before sending notifications and respect later system choices, including silencing. Some locales exempt government alerts from complete silencing. Notifications can remain available even while Focus delays their alerts. ## Integrating with Focus Focus filters interruption by activity and allowed contacts/apps; scheduled summaries defer alerts to selected times. Communication notifications use sender-based decisions through supported SiriKit intents. Assign an interruption level to other notifications: | Level | Intended urgency | Scheduled delivery override | Focus breakthrough | Silent override | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Passive | Leisurely information | No | No | No | | Active | Ordinary timely update; default | No | No | No | | Time Sensitive | Direct immediate personal impact | Yes | Yes | No | | Critical | Urgent health/safety need | Yes | Yes | Yes | Critical requires an entitlement because it can override delivery, Focus, and silent settings. People can choose whether Time Sensitive alerts break through. ## Best practices Assign urgency honestly to preserve trust. Time Sensitive belongs to events happening now or within an hour, not merely content the app wants noticed. The system introduces and periodically re-evaluates this permission with the person, who can turn it off. ## Sending marketing notifications Send promotions only after an explicit opt-in describing the content with a clear accept/decline choice. Never classify marketing as Time Sensitive. Provide an in-app notification settings screen so people can change informational and marketing preferences. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or visionOS rules are specified. ### watchOS Watch generally inherits the companion iPhone's notification settings. People can change them in the iPhone Watch app or through per-notification actions after a left swipe, such as temporary mute or disabling Time Sensitive alerts. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Privacy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) #### Developer documentation #### Videos

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

# Writing Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Treat language as an integral interface element in onboarding, alerts, accessibility descriptions, and ordinary tasks. ## Getting started Choose a consistent voice based on the audience, familiar vocabulary, and desired feeling; maintain a terminology list. Adjust tone to the situation, such as a serious payment failure versus an achievement celebration, without changing identity. Remove unnecessary words and read copy aloud to test clarity. Use plain, nongendered, localizable wording and consider screen-reader access. ## Best practices - Start each screen with its most important information. Format for scanning and divide unrelated ideas or complex sequences across suitable screens. - Label actions with clear verbs and links with their actual destination/purpose, avoiding clever substitutes or generic click-here wording. Establish reusable wording and capitalization patterns appropriate to each component type. - Make multistep flows consistent: entry, continuation, and completion should be clear from labels. Minimize unnecessary my/your possessives and avoid switching perspectives; vague we statements obscure responsibility, especially in errors. - Name the correct input action for each device. Small watch/phone displays and distant/shared TVs all benefit from brevity; consider everyone who can see a shared screen. - Give empty states a useful next action, preferably a button/link, without placing essential permanent instructions in a transient state. - Prevent errors first. When needed, place concise, blame-free messages near the problem and explain a concrete remedy. Avoid flippant interjections and vague invalid-value labels. Reconsider the interaction if many people repeatedly hit the same error. - Choose alerts, notifications, sheets, or inline guidance according to urgency, context, required action, and explanation length. - Use practical settings labels. Explain the enabled behavior when necessary and link directly to the setting rather than describing a navigation route. - Label all text fields. Add format hints/examples and nearby correction guidance that tells people what to enter instead of merely listing prohibitions. ## Platform considerations No additional platform-specific rules are provided. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: December 16, 2025, February 27, 2023.

item.text: The supplied brief identifies four defects: diagnosis disclosure, repeated interruptions, an unrelated destination, and acknowledgment canceling the appointment. I’ll specify generic notification content, one reminder per appointment occurrence, a direct appointment link, and acknowledgment that changes only reminder state. I’ll also define the permission-denied path.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > interface.md <<'EOF'
# iPhone appointment reminder specification

Platform: iOS, standard system notification. This replaces the prior behavior that exposed a full diagnosis on the Lock Screen, repeated every minute after dismissal, opened Home, and canceled an appointment when acknowledged. Notification permission may be denied.

## Content and privacy

Use these exact English strings in every notification presentation, including unlocked banners and expanded notifications:

- Title: "'`Appointment Reminder`
- Body: `You have an upcoming appointment.`
- Preview-hidden category description: `Appointment reminder` (system presentation and preview settings remain authoritative).
- One optional notification action: `Acknowledge`.

Do not include diagnosis, patient name, clinician, specialty, location, date/time, attachments, or medical imagery in notification content. The system supplies app identity; do not repeat it in the title/body. Generic wording even with previews enabled is a deliberate privacy choice. Appointment details, including localized date/time and time zone, are available only inside the app after the existing account authentication gate. Do not put sensitive information in deep-link URLs or logs; use an opaque appointment identifier and verify ownership before resolving it. An opaque identifier is not authorization. No new health-data access or collection is required by this change.

## Delivery and permission

Product default: one reminder 24 hours before the appointment occurrence, only when the person enables appointment reminders and system authorization permits delivery. If enabled less than 24 hours before an upcoming appointment, schedule one reminder immediately; do not send for appointments already started. These timing choices are product policy, not HIG requirements. Use ordinary Active interruption; no Time Sensitive or Critical escalation, no bypass of Focus, summary, silence, or preview choices. Delivery and presentation are never guaranteed.

Ask for system notification permission when the person first selects `Enable Reminders` in appointment settings, not automatically at launch. The settings explanation is `Receive a reminder before each appointment.` Use the actual system authorization prompt; no imitation or custom pre-permission alert. Booking, appointment access, and cancellation remain available without notification consent.

- Not determined: that explicit selection invokes the system request.
- Authorized: schedule eligible reminders while the in-app preference is on.
- Denied or subsequently revoked: do not retry the authorization prompt or send catch-up reminders. Show `Notifications are off. View upcoming appointments here or change notification access in Settings.` in appointment settings, with `Open Settings` and an always-available `Upcoming Appointments` route. Recheck authorization on return and reconcile future eligible schedules.
- Quiet/provisional or other restricted authorization: honor the granted scope and system presentation; do not claim alerts or sound are enabled.
- In-app preference off: remove pending appointment reminders and their delivered entries; appointments remain unchanged.

## Event identity and state

Separate appointment status (`scheduled`, `canceled`, or current server status) from reminder status (`pending`, `issued`, `viewed`, `acknowledged`, `dismissed`, `expired`). `issued` means submitted for system delivery, not proof the person saw it. Persist reminder identity by account + appointment occurrence + reminder policy; a delivery retry must reuse that identity. One occurrence has one reminder under this policy.

| Event | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Eligible scheduled occurrence | Create one pending reminder. Atomically record issuance so retries cannot create another reminder. |
| No response, system dismissal, or acknowledgment | Never create another reminder for that occurrence. Remove the every-minute repeat behavior. Dismissal changes reminder state only when observable; no repeat depends on receiving a dismissal callback. |
| Appointment rescheduled before issuance | Replace its pending schedule using the same occurrence identity and revised time. |
| Appointment rescheduled after issuance | Remove stale delivered content; show the current time in the app. Do not issue a second reminder for that occurrence. |
| Appointment canceled, started, or deleted | Remove pending/delivered reminder; suppress stale delivery and acknowledgment work. |
| Duplicate event/action or process restart | Reconcile persisted state idempotently; never repeat interruption or mutate appointment status. |
| Sign-out/account switch | Remove that account'"'s pending/delivered reminders; never resolve a link in another account. |

Revalidate current appointment state before issuance or action handling when available. If an offline queued reminder slips through after a remote change, activation must fetch current state before presenting it as scheduled. Do not claim atomic control over remote updates and system delivery.

## Activation and actions

Ordinary notification activation opens that exact appointment's detail screen, preserving the destination through sign-in/unlock. Do not open generic Home or add an "'`Open App` notification action. Fetch the current appointment and verify the active account. If canceled, show its current canceled state; if missing or inaccessible, show `This appointment is no longer available.` with `Upcoming Appointments`. Do not show cached medical details to an unverified account.

`Acknowledge` marks only the identified reminder acknowledged and removes its pending/delivered notification. Require authentication before resolving this health-related action. Preserve the action through authentication; if authentication is canceled, leave acknowledgment uncommitted. Repeat activation is harmless. It must never invoke appointment cancellation, change booking status, or imply attendance confirmation. Feedback inside the app: `Reminder acknowledged. Your appointment is unchanged.` On persistence failure, show `Couldn’t acknowledge the reminder. Try again.` with `Try Again`; do not report success.

System dismissal clears only the notification presentation and, if observable, records dismissal. Opening details marks the reminder viewed and removes its notification. No notification action cancels an appointment; any existing appointment cancellation flow remains separate inside authenticated appointment details.

## Foreground and badges

When the app is active, update the relevant appointment row/details quietly rather than presenting a duplicate banner, sound, or modal. Keep `Upcoming Appointments` discoverable regardless of permission or badge settings. This reminder feature sets no app-icon badge; do not display appointment counts or clinical values as badges or overwrite another feature'"'s unread count. Essential meaning is conveyed in text without sound.

## Acceptance contract

Verify both logic and native presentation before release:

1. Locked, preview-hidden, preview-visible, expanded, and unlocked presentations contain only the specified generic text; no diagnosis or identifying appointment details appear.
2. Issue, dismiss, wait several minutes, restart, and replay the event: no second reminder. Rescheduling follows the before/after-issuance rules.
3. Activate with two appointments present: the matching current appointment opens, including after authentication; wrong-account, deleted, canceled, and offline cases never reveal unauthorized or falsely current details.
4. Acknowledge twice: reminder acknowledged once, notification removed, and appointment status/booking unchanged. Canceled authentication and write failure do not report success.
5. Deny/revoke authorization, disable reminders, and return from Settings: appointment access persists, no prompt loop or catch-up flood occurs, and eligible future schedules reconcile.
6. Focus, summary, silent mode, and disabled previews remain respected; no guaranteed-delivery wording appears.
7. Foreground arrival updates the app without duplicate interruption; no badge is introduced. Read the content and action with VoiceOver and check actual system truncation/localization on an iPhone.

## Design basis

Local installed HIG snapshot consulted; links identify source sections, not a claim of online verification:

- [Notifications: best practices, content, actions, badging](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/notifications): confidentiality, concise content, no repeat for nonresponse, contextual activation, useful nondestructive actions, foreground treatment.
- [Managing notifications: integrating with Focus](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications#Integrating-with-Focus): consent, honest urgency, system control.
- [Privacy: requesting permission and protecting data](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy): contextual access and protection. Generic content and authenticated acknowledgment are conservative product choices.
- [Writing: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing#Best-practices): clear outcome labels and actionable recovery copy.
EOF"

# Result

Patched "'`interface.md` in place with an implementable iPhone reminder contract. Replaced diagnosis disclosure with exact generic title/body and hidden-preview copy; removed every-minute repeats; specified appointment-specific activation; separated acknowledgment from booking cancellation; and added permission-denied recovery, event identity, foreground behavior, badge policy, and acceptance checks.

## Decisions and support

- Keep notification content generic even when unlocked. [Notifications — Best practices and Content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/notifications#Content) supports protecting confidential content and generic hidden previews. Omitting appointment time and provider is this specification'"'s conservative privacy choice.
- Send one reminder per occurrence; dismissal and nonresponse never trigger another. [Notifications — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/notifications#Best-practices) advises against repeating the same event for nonresponse. A 24-hour lead time and no second reminder after rescheduling an issued occurrence are explicit product choices.
- Activation resolves the correct appointment; "'`Acknowledge` changes reminder state only. [Notification actions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/notifications#Notification-actions) supports useful, clearly labeled, preferably nondestructive actions without redundant Open App. Authentication before acknowledgment is an added product safeguard.
- Request permission in context, preserve appointment access when denied, and use Active urgency. [Managing notifications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-notifications#Integrating-with-Focus) supports consent and honest interruption levels; no evidence justifies Critical delivery. [Privacy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Requesting-permission) supports contextual permission requests and minimized access.
- Use explicit success/failure wording and a recovery action, following [Writing](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing#Best-practices). Quiet foreground updates and no new badge follow the notification guidance; badges are optional, not required.

## Worked before/after

Illustrative fixture, not an observed payload: appointment A is tomorrow at 10:00; appointment B is next week. A has a confidential diagnosis in its authenticated record.

| Step | Before, based on supplied brief | Revised specification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A'"'s reminder appears | Full diagnosis visible on Lock Screen; exact original text not supplied | "'`Appointment Reminder` / `You have an upcoming appointment.` Hidden-preview description: `Appointment reminder`. |
| Person dismisses it | Reappears every minute | No repeat for A, including after retry or restart. |
| Person activates it | Opens generic Home | Authenticate if needed, then open A'"'s current details, never B. |
| Person chooses acknowledgment | Cancels A | Marks A's reminder acknowledged; booking remains scheduled. Feedback: "'`Reminder acknowledged. Your appointment is unchanged.` |
| Permission denied | Failure behavior unspecified | No prompt loop; upcoming appointments remain accessible, with an optional Settings route. |

## Acceptance audit

Passed — static specification review: all four supplied defects have explicit replacements in `interface.md`; denied/revoked permission has a usable fallback; exact strings, identity and duplicate rules, stale/account states, action failure, foreground handling, and badge policy are defined. The worked fixture traces the intended outcomes, not executed behavior.

Failed — no static specification checks remain failed. This does not establish that an implementation passes.

Not executed — actual notification generation, delivery, deduplication under concurrency, persistence failure, deep-link routing, account authorization, system permission prompts, Focus/summary/silent behavior, hidden-preview rendering, SDK compilation, device/GUI testing, localization, truncation, and VoiceOver. The numbered acceptance contract in `interface.md` defines checks for an implementation before release.

## Evidence and routing limits

Explicitly read the installed root `.agents/skills/apple-hig/SKILL.md`, then the System experiences family and Notifications procedure; searched the complete topic index for notification, privacy, and writing concepts. Read the Patterns family and Managing notifications procedure, and Foundations family with Privacy and Writing procedures, before reading their respective source guides. Each file was consumed by its own `cat` command; the index search used its own `rg` command. All paths were resolved within this installed package.

Sources were supplied `interface.md` and the installed local guidance only.
